chapter: Mingus and the call from Hampton
title: The note at Henri's: Lionel Hampton wants him
summary: At Henri's club on Indiana Avenue, Monk was handed a message to call Hampton, who wanted him in San Francisco.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Well, when you joined the band, actually joined it, wasn't there some reading involved?

No, that was funny too because I remember when I came, I was working in a place called Henri's. Henri's was on our little Strip there, Indiana Avenue, and it was the jazz club. It was the jazz club, you know. It had built a reputation like...the in crowd knew about Henri's. It was the place, then. We were working there at Henri's and when I got to work that night, there was a message for me that Henri, the guy that owned the joint, gave me this note.

And when I got there everybody was all up in the air waiting for me to come in. I came a little early and I was wondering what was going on and then he handed me this note. And he said, 'I want you to call this number. Call that number right away because Lionel Hampton wants you to join his band.' So I'm saying, 'These cats are putting me on.' I just wouldn't hear it. And they were very serious, and everybody's really up about it.

And I came in, thought about it, the more nervous I begin to get because I guess it was what guys usually do, contact somebody when they need somebody. I couldn't understand why he was calling me. That's what threw me. Why me? And then, knowing Henri's like I did, he really got serious and I knew he was serious because he knew Hamp. Hamp was in town, he stayed at Henri's brother's house or something like that. Anyhow, he convinced me that he was serious and Hamp really wanted me to call him.

I didn't get ahold of Hamp; I tried that night, it didn't do any good. And that next morning I got ahold of him. He said yeah, he wanted me to join the band right away if I could and it was in San Francisco. Wanted me to fly out to San Francisco. I'd never been on a plane, I'd never been any further than Chicago, which was less than 200 miles away, and Columbus the other way. And here I was talking about going to the West Coast to join Lionel Hampton's band...
